Thank you, Eduarda. I read the deck last night. Could you tell me what your base case is?
Our base case is a price of a hundred and five million. That's about nine and a half times Lane's yearly profit.
That's well above NorthPack's first offer. I'd like to know why they would pay that much.
Because NorthPack is a buyer that needs Lane's factories. What they're paying for is capacity they can't build in three years.
Fine. Now let me grill you on the risks. Is the supplier case covered?
Yes. If Lane loses the case, NorthPack is entitled to take the loss from the escrow.

Hi Eduarda, it's Richard. The investment committee meets at ten tomorrow, so here is how it works. You will present the deck for ten minutes, and then the members will grill you for twenty. David Moore is the one who asks the hardest questions, so be ready for him. We need a majority, not a unanimous vote, but a unanimous vote sends a strong message. If a member has a conflict of interest, he or she abstains. And remember: the committee doesn't only vote on the numbers. They also vote on your conviction. See you there.

An investment committee is the group that decides whether a firm goes ahead with a deal. Many presenters think that the numbers are what matters most. In my experience, it's the risks that the committee wants to discuss. So put your base case on one slide and your risks on the next one. Don't wait for the committee to find the problems. Show them first. If a member disagrees with you, don't fight. Listen to the dissent, and ask what would change their mind. Sometimes the answer is a conditional approval: the deal goes ahead, but only if a condition is met. That is not a failure. It is how good committees work.

Richard left Eduarda a voicemail the day before the investment committee. The next morning, Eduarda presented the deck in ten minutes. Then David Moore grilled her on the risks. He wasn't sure about the fifteen percent cap. Eduarda explained that it's the escrow that protects the firm. In the end, the committee gave a conditional approval.
